questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is divisible by $2$?

options.why: Looked at the digits inside the number rather than the last digit.
Assumed a number ending in $5$ can still be halved into two whole numbers.
Treated the number as even because its first digit is $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$1112$ ends in $2$, which is even, so it is divisible by $2$.
The other numbers end in $3$, $5$ and $7$, which are all odd.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is divisible by $4$?

options.why: Checked only the last digit $4$ instead of the last two digits $94$.
Checked only that the number is even, which is the test for $2$, not $4$.
Used the digit sum, which is the test for $3$, not for $4$.

questions.solution_text:
The last two digits of $532$ are $32$.
$32\div 4=8$
So $532$ is divisible by $4$. The last two digits of the others are $94$, $42$ and $06$, none of which divide by $4$.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is divisible by $3$?

options.why: Assumed any number containing a $3$ is divisible by $3$.
Looked at the first digit instead of adding all the digits.
Checked the last digit rather than the sum of the digits.

questions.solution_text:
$8+3+0+1$
$=12$
$12$ is divisible by $3$, so $8301$ is. The digit sums of the others are $13$, $17$ and $25$.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is divisible by $10$?

options.why: Used the test for $5$, where a last digit of $5$ is also allowed.
Checked only that the number is even, which is the test for $2$, not $10$.
Assumed a number beginning with $10$ is divisible by $10$.

questions.solution_text:
$13\,330$ ends in $0$, so it is divisible by $10$.
The others end in $5$, $4$ and $1$.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is divisible by $6$?

options.why: Checked the digit sum for $3$ but not that the number is even.
Checked that the number is even but not the digit sum for $3$.

questions.solution_text:
$35\,730$ ends in $0$, so it is divisible by $2$.
$3+5+7+3+0$
$=18$
$18$ is divisible by $3$, so $35\,730$ is divisible by $6$. $1809$ is odd, and the digit sum of $578$ is $20$.

questions.question_text: Which pair of divisibility tests correctly checks whether a number is divisible by $20$?

options.why: These multiply to $20$ but share the factor $2$, so passing both is not enough.
These multiply to $10$, so the pair only checks divisibility by $10$.

questions.solution_text: $20=4\times 5$, and $4$ and $5$ have no common factor, so testing for $4$ and for $5$ checks divisibility by $20$.

options.why: Assumed a number divisible by $2$ and $10$ must also be divisible by $4$, without testing the last two digits.
Read only the last digit and never added the digits to test for $3$ and $6$.
Applied the single-digit tests but did not combine $2$ and $3$ to get $6$ or check the final zero for $10$.

questions.solution_text:
The last digit is $0$, so $1\,308\,150$ is divisible by $2$, $5$ and $10$.
$1+3+0+8+1+5+0$
$=18$
So it is divisible by $3$, and being even as well, by $6$.
The last two digits are $50$, which is not divisible by $4$.

questions.question_text: What is the largest three-digit number divisible by both $6$ and $10$?

options.why: Applied only the test for $6$ and took the largest three-digit multiple of $6$.
Used the test for $5$ instead of the test for $10$, allowing a last digit of $5$.
Dropped to a round hundred instead of testing numbers downwards from $999$.

questions.solution_text:
To be divisible by $10$ the last digit must be $0$, so the candidates are $990$, $980$, $970$, and so on.
$9+9+0$
$=18$
$18$ is divisible by $3$, and $990$ is even, so $990$ is divisible by $6$.
The largest such number is $990$.

questions.question_text: For which value of the digit $\square$ is $54\square$ divisible by both $3$ and $4$?

options.why: Made the digit sum $12$ pass the test for $3$ and stopped, without testing for $4$ at all.
Tested the last two digits $44$ for $4$ but never added the digits to test for $3$.
Passed the test for $3$ with digit sum $15$, then checked only that the number is even instead of testing the last two digits $46$ for $4$.

questions.solution_text:
$54\square$ is divisible by $4$ when the last two digits $4\square$ are $40$, $44$ or $48$, so $\square=0$, $4$ or $8$.
$5+4+\square$
$=9+\square$
$9+\square$ is divisible by $3$ when $\square=0$, $3$, $6$ or $9$.
The only digit in both lists is $0$.
